q: 1. According to I.S.: 456, the thickness of R.C.C. footing on soils at its edges is kept not less than ...........
explain: To ensure durability and proper cover, IS:456 specifies a minimum edge thickness of 150 mm for footings on soil.

q: 2. According to I.S.: 456, the thickness at the edge on top of piles for a footing on the piles should not be less than ...........
explain: For footings on piles, the minimum edge thickness is increased to 300 mm due to the higher concentrated loads from piles.

q: 3. If the width of the foundation for two columns is restricted, the shape of the footing generally adopted is ...........
explain: A trapezoidal combined footing is used when the load of one column is much higher than the other and the width of the footing is restricted.

q: 4. A raft foundation is provided if the areas of the foundation exceeds the plan area of the building by ...........
explain: If individual footings cover more than 50% of the building area, a raft (mat) foundation is usually more economical and safer.

q: 5. A foundation rests on ...........
explain: Subgrade and foundation soil are terms used to describe the natural or prepared ground that supports the foundation load.

q: 6. The centre to centre spacing of vertical stirrups, in a rectangular beam, is ............
explain: Shear force is maximum at the supports and minimum at the center. Therefore, stirrups are placed closer together at the ends and the spacing is increased toward the center.

q: 7. The main reinforcement in R.C.C. cantilever members is placed at
explain: In a cantilever beam, tension occurs at the top because it bends downward (hogging moment). Therefore, main reinforcement must be at the top.

q: 8. The main reinforcement in R.C.C simply supported member is placed at
explain: A simply supported beam under gravity loads experiences sagging (tension at the bottom), so reinforcement is placed in the bottom fibre.

q: 9. The main reinforcement in R.C.C. continuous members is placed at
explain: Continuous beams experience sagging (bottom tension) in the span and hogging (top tension) at the supports, requiring reinforcement at both top and bottom.

q: 10. The aspect ratio is defined as the ratio of
options: length to breadth of a slab
effective width of flange and effective depth of the beam
width of web and depth of flange
explain: Aspect ratio (ly/lx) is the ratio of the longer span to the shorter span of a slab, used to determine if it is one-way or two-way.

q: 11. The intermediate beams between several beams case monolithically with the slab
explain: Beams cast monolithically with a slab act as T-beams when they have slabs on both sides (intermediate) and L-beams on the ends.

q: 12. When the ratio of the long to short dimensions of the slab in greater than X, the slab may be designed as one-way slab where X is
explain: If Ly/Lx > 2.0, the slab primarily bends in the shorter direction and is designed as a one-way slab.

q: 13. The minimum percentage of high yield strength deformed reinforcement bars (H.Y.S.D.) provided in R.C.C. slabs is
explain: For HYSD bars, the minimum reinforcement is 0.12% of the gross area. (For mild steel, it is 0.15%).

q: 14. A reinforced concrete slab is 75 mm thick. The maximum size of reinforcement bar that can be used is
explain: Max diameter = Thickness / 8 = 75 / 8 = 9.375 mm. The standard bar size below this is 8 mm.

q: 15. If the sides of a slab simply supported on its edges and spanning in two ways are equal, then the maximum bending moment is multiplied by
explain: For a square slab, the load is shared equally, effectively halving the moment compared to a one-way span of the same length.

q: 16. The drop are provided in flat slabs to resist
explain: Drops (thickened portions of the slab) are primarily provided to increase the slab's resistance to punching shear at the column connection.

q: 17. When a circular slab simply supported at the edge is loaded with uniformly distributed load, the stresses are developed in
explain: A loaded circular slab experiences bending in all directions, resulting in both radial and circumferential (hoop) moments and stresses.

q: 18. For a circular slab carrying a uniformly distributed load, the ratio of maximum negative radial moment and the maximum positive radial moment is equal to
explain: For a circular slab with fixed edges, the ratio of the negative moment at the support to the positive moment at the center is 2.0.

q: 19. The thickness of the topping of a ribbed slab is kept from
explain: The topping (the thin slab on top of the ribs) typically varies between 50 mm to 80 mm depending on the spacing of the ribs.

q: 20. In a ribbed slab, the clear spacing between the ribs should not be more than
explain: Standard practice limits the clear spacing between ribs to 450 mm to ensure the topping slab can span between them effectively.

q: 21. Thickened part of the flat slab over its supporting column is known as
explain: The drop panel is the portion of the slab that is thickened around the column to resist high shear and negative moments.

q: 22. The lap length of a direct, tension reinforcement bar in a R.C.C. beams should be more than
options: 30 times the diameter of the bar
twice the development length or 30 times the diameter of the bar
48 times the diameter of the bar
24 times the diameter of the bar or development length
explain: For direct tension, the lap length is taken as 2Ld or 30φ, whichever is greater, to ensure safety against sudden failure.

q: 23. The minimum horizontal distance between two main reinforcement bars should be
options: diameter of the larger bar or 5 mm more than the nominal maximum size of coarse aggregate
5 mm more than the nominal size of the aggregate
5 mm more than the diameter of the bar
size of the aggregate of 5 mm more than the diameter of the bars
explain: To allow concrete to flow between bars, the gap must be at least the diameter of the bar or 5 mm more than the aggregate size.

q: 24. The minimum cover to the main bars in R.C.C. beam must be
options: 15 mm or diameter of the bar
25 mm or diameter of the bar
40 mm or diameter of the bar
25 mm or size of the coarse aggregate
explain: For beams, a nominal cover of 25 mm or the bar diameter (whichever is greater) is standard for moderate exposure.

q: 25. The minimum cover to the reinforcement of precast concrete piles is
explain: Piles are buried in soil (aggressive environment), requiring a higher cover of at least 40 mm.

q: 26. The pitch of the main bars in a simply supported slab, should not exceed its effective depth by
explain: IS 456 specifies that the maximum spacing (pitch) for main tension reinforcement in slabs must not exceed 3 times the effective depth (3d) or 300 mm.

q: 27. The amount of reinforcement for main bars in a slab, is based upon
explain: Design reinforcement is always calculated to resist the maximum bending moment occurring at any critical section of the slab.

q: 28. In a slab, the pitch of the main reinforcement should not exceed its effective depth
explain: To ensure proper load distribution and crack control, the spacing of main bars is limited to 3 times the effective depth.

q: 29. If the diameter of the main reinforcement in a slab is 16 mm, the concrete cover to main bars is
explain: Nominal cover should generally not be less than the diameter of the bar (16 mm in this case) or the specified environmental cover (usually 15-20mm for slabs).

q: 30. The maximum permissible size of aggregate to be used in casing the ribs of a slab, is
explain: In ribbed slabs with thin sections, 10 mm aggregate is used to ensure the concrete can flow around the closely spaced reinforcement.

q: 31. An R.C.C roof slab is designed as a two way slab if
options: it supports loads in both directions
the ratio of spans in two directions is less than 2
the slab is continuous over two supports
the slab is discontinuous at edges
explain: If the aspect ratio (long span / short span) is less than 2, the slab significantly bends in both directions and must be designed as a two-way slab.
